answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer: No, please do not do that. Two rules after a fever: wait until you have been fever-free for a few days before running again (you have), and do not try to replace missed sessions, because the body is still recovering even once the temperature is normal. We ease back in with a walk, then one short walk-run, then build from there. The race is 8 weeks away, which is plenty of runway, so losing one week changes nothing about getting you to the start line ready to run the whole way.

new.analysis:
## How I read the week

You ran Monday as planned and sensibly stopped there once the cold turned into a fever on Wednesday night. That is the right call, not a failure, and the Monday run itself looked steady at the same pattern you have been doing.

## Why next week looks like this

The guidance after a fever is to come back below where you left off, not at it or above it. So Monday is a walk, not a run, to see how your chest and energy feel moving at pace. Wednesday is a shorter walk-run than before (6 run blocks instead of 8), and Saturday returns to the 24-minute session you did two weeks ago rather than the 27 minutes that was planned.

## The bigger picture

You have 8 weeks until Corrowmore. If this coming week goes well, the week after we go back to building, and you will still have 6 weeks to grow the running blocks from 2 minutes toward continuous running. There is no need to chase the missed sessions.

If the cough is still there by the weekend, or at any point you feel short of breath, tight-chested or dizzy on a run, please stop and get it checked before the next session.

safetyCallouts.title: Returning after a fever.
safetyCallouts.body: You had a temperature of 38.4 midweek and are still coughing and congested. Please see a GP if the cough is not clearing, you feel breathless, your chest hurts, your heart races at rest, or you feel unusually tired after easy effort. Stop the session and walk home if any of these show up while running.
